VentureViz: who funded whom, month by month

A force-directed map of AI startups and their investors that can replay how the web formed, one month at a time, with a camera that follows the new funding rounds.

The problem

Funding news arrives one headline at a time, so the shape of it is hard to see. Which investors back several of the same companies, and in what order did the connections form?

I wanted a page where you can drag the network around and also press play and watch it grow. The data is small and hand-collected, 8 companies and 75 funding entries, so the work is in the interface.

How it works

  1. Load and check the data.A pure module validates every month as YYYY-MM and builds a read-only model.
  2. Turn it into beats.One beat per month with activity: foundings land first, then deals, then the beat settles. Pure functions answer "what has happened by time t", so scrubbing is instant.
  3. Run one frame loop.A single d3 timer advances the playhead, updates the graph, steps the camera and the HUD together.
  4. Keep nodes alive.Keyed joins mean the network grows in place instead of reshuffling, and a spring camera frames what is about to appear.

Drag a node in the figure, or move the date slider to watch rounds appear. The full timeline replay lives on the live site.

Results

There is no accuracy to report, so here is what exists. The README describes a 50 second replay at 1x, speeds from 0.5x to 4x, a scrubber with month previews, filtering, keyboard control and a reduced-motion mode. Tests run with Node's built-in test runner and cover the data, schedule, camera, HUD and the details panel's HTML escaping.

Source: the repository README and data/ai_startups_timeline.json.

Limits and next steps

  • 8 companies is a small slice of the market. The data was collected by hand and I have not checked it against a funding database.
  • Investor names are used as written, so "Lightspeed" and "Lightspeed Venture Partners" are two nodes, and the 56 includes such pairs.
  • It needs a web server, because browsers block ES modules and fetch() from file://. The page says so.
  • Next: merge duplicate investor names and grow the dataset.
